findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:459 — usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` blindly trusts that when the `GROUPS` session attribute was set, the underlying `searchForUserStream` datastore implementation actually applied it as a hard filter; if any user-store provider (e.g. a federated/custom UserStorageProvider) ignores the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute during search, `grantIfNoPermission(true)` would cause `canView(user)` to rubber-stamp every returned user as viewable with no independent per-user check, silently exposing users outside the caller's granted groups — this trust boundary is unchanged from V1 behavior but is now exercised for both GroupPermissions and GroupPermissionsV2 code paths without a corresponding assertion that the group filter was truly enforced at the storage layer

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:656 — hasPermission() falls back to the shared "all-groups" type-resource (and evaluates using that resource's full scope set) whenever no per-group resource exists, so a policy attached to the all-groups resource for one scope (e.g. VIEW) can be evaluated together with unrelated scopes it does not grant; verify evaluatePermission does not leak scopes not explicitly matched by policy for the resource-type case

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:299 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() short-circuits to empty set when root.users().canView() is true, and the old canManage() OR-branch was removed; verified this is intentional (canManage-only admins fall through to per-group hasPermission evaluation) and callers (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource) correctly branch on usersEvaluator.canView() separately before calling this, so no over-restriction found, but the removal of the canManage() shortcut means canManage()-only admins now pay for an extra resourceStore scan per request that canView() admins skip for free — flagging as a low-severity behavior-change note rather than a confirmed vulnerability

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:177 — Removed short-circuit `canViewGlobal \|\| auth.groups().canView(g)` filter for listing subgroups, now always calling `auth.groups()::canView` per group — no test verifies behavioral/performance parity for an admin holding a global (all-groups) VIEW permission when listing many subgroups (each call now re-evaluates hasPermission per group instead of skipping via the global flag)

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:112 — Same removal of the `canViewGlobal` short-circuit in the top-level groups listing filter; no test covers many-groups + all-groups-view-permission scenario to confirm identical results (and no perf/N+1-evaluation regression) compared to pre-change behavior

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:459 — usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` blindly trusts that when the `GROUPS` session attribute was set, the underlying `searchForUserStream` datastore implementation actually applied it as a hard filter; if any user-store provider (e.g. a federated/custom UserStorageProvider) ignores the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute during search, `grantIfNoPermission(true)` would cause `canView(user)` to rubber-stamp every returned user as viewable with no independent per-user check, silently exposing users outside the caller's granted groups — this trust boundary is unchanged from V1 behavior but is now exercised for both GroupPermissions and GroupPermissionsV2 code paths without a corresponding assertion that the group filter was truly enforced at the storage layer

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser` the diff removes the explicit per-user permission filter: `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced with passing the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` directly into `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, the method relies on setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (now via `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`) as the mechanism to constrain results when the caller lacks global view. This increases/creates reliance on the underlying `UserProvider`/user-store honoring the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute as a hard filter; if a provider ignores it, users outside permitted groups could flow through without the previously-present `usersEvaluator::canView` stream filter. The finding’s mention of `grantIfNoPermission(...)` can’t be verified from the shown hunk, but the diff-grounded removal of the filter makes the described exposure plausible and is a security/correctness regression unless `toRepresentation` independently filters (not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:656 — hasPermission() falls back to the shared "all-groups" type-resource (and evaluates using that resource's full scope set) whenever no per-group resource exists, so a policy attached to the all-groups resource for one scope (e.g. VIEW) can be evaluated together with unrelated scopes it does not grant; verify evaluatePermission does not leak scopes not explicitly matched by policy for the resource-type case

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2#hasPermission(...)`, when a per-group `Resource` is not found (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null), it falls back to the resource-type resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and then evaluates permissions using `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)`, i.e., passing the full scope set for that type-resource. While the method later filters returned `Permission` objects by `expectedScopes`, the diff does not show how `root.evaluatePermission(...)` computes/returns scopes for this resource-type case, so it’s not verifiable from the diff whether unrelated scopes could be returned/"leaked". Still, the concern is diff-grounded and nontrivial: evaluating with all scopes instead of only the requested `scopes` increases the risk of broader-than-intended authorization outcomes depending on the underlying authorization engine behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:299 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() short-circuits to empty set when root.users().canView() is true, and the old canManage() OR-branch was removed; verified this is intentional (canManage-only admins fall through to per-group hasPermission evaluation) and callers (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource) correctly branch on usersEvaluator.canView() separately before calling this, so no over-restriction found, but the removal of the canManage() shortcut means canManage()-only admins now pay for an extra resourceStore scan per request that canView() admins skip for free — flagging as a low-severity behavior-change note rather than a confirmed vulnerability

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` changed its early return from `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()` to only `root.users().canView()`. However, in this PR `root.users().canView()` (see `UserPermissions.canView()`) explicitly returns true for admins with `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` as well, so a “canManage-only admin” does not actually fall through to the resourceStore scan based on what’s visible in the diff. Also, the finding claims callers now “branch on usersEvaluator.canView() separately before calling this”, but `UsersResource.searchForUser()` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser()` now call `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` unconditionally; the short-circuit happens inside that method, not in the caller. The alleged added per-request resourceStore scan cost for manage-only admins is therefore not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:177 — Removed short-circuit `canViewGlobal \|\| auth.groups().canView(g)` filter for listing subgroups, now always calling `auth.groups()::canView` per group — no test verifies behavioral/performance parity for an admin holding a global (all-groups) VIEW permission when listing many subgroups (each call now re-evaluates hasPermission per group instead of skipping via the global flag)

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResource#getSubGroups the diff replaces `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView(); ... filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))` with `filter(auth.groups()::canView)`, removing the one-time global short-circuit (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java). Given the new fine-grained logic in GroupPermissionsV2, `canView(GroupModel)` directly evaluates permissions per group (`hasPermission(group.getId(), VIEW, MANAGE)`) and does not consult `canView()`/a cached global check, so an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission may now incur per-subgroup permission evaluation. The added tests (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest) cover listing groups and all-groups VIEW/MANAGE, but do not exercise subgroup listing behavior under global permissions or guard against this regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:112 — Same removal of the `canViewGlobal` short-circuit in the top-level groups listing filter; no test covers many-groups + all-groups-view-permission scenario to confirm identical results (and no perf/N+1-evaluation regression) compared to pre-change behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `GroupsResource.getGroups` removes the one-time `canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView()` short-circuit and replaces `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` with `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`, which will invoke per-group evaluation (`canView(GroupModel)`) for every returned group. With the newly introduced V2 evaluator (`GroupPermissionsV2`), `canView()` can check the “all-groups” permission once, while `canView(group)` may do per-group permission/resource lookups, so the change plausibly risks N+1/perf regression even if functional results are identical. The added `testViewGroups` covers the all-groups VIEW permission only with 2 groups and does not exercise a many-groups scenario to detect behavioral parity under scale or guard against per-item evaluation costs.
